name: JavaScript
description: JavaScript, often abbreviated as JS, is a high-level, interpreted programming language that conforms to the ECMAScript specification. It is a language which is also characterized as dynamic, weakly typed, prototype-based and multi-paradigm.
pointDescription: Basic knowledge CSS and HTML. Saw a code once.
Intermediate knowledge of both HTML and CSS. Variables and how to declare them. Know operators, like +, -, etc.

Know the functions. What an API is. How to access and query the DOM.Understand loops. Create and render new elements on to the DOM.How and when JS renders on a web page. Know the events. How to listen for events and create your own.

Function and variable scopes, you should know what this is. Anonymous functions and Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE). Browser support for new JS features and how to use polyfills to fill in support when needed

How to make an AJAX request. How to use promises and know when you get data. The differences in var, let, and const to declare variables. What closures are and how to utilize them. What Object-Oriented Programming, or OOP, is and how it can happen in Javascript. Optimization of logic for speed.

trainings.name: HTML Basics
trainings.shortDescription: HTML Crash Course For Absolute Beginners

name: Machine Learning
description: Machine learning (ML) is a field of artificial intelligence that uses statistical techniques to give computer systems the ability to 'learn' (e.g., progressively improve performance on a specific task) from data, without being explicitly programmed.
pointDescription: Understanding the entire ecosystem that you’re designing for. You know how to program like Python.
Understanding statistics, especially Bayesian probability, is essential for many machine learning algorithms
Machine learning is an exceptionally wide and interdisciplinary field that consolidates linear algebra, statistics, hacking skills, database skills, and distributed computing skills.
Knows distributed systems for large data: MPI, Grid Engine.
Ununderstand how the different pieces work together, communicate with them (using library calls, REST APIs, database queries, etc.) and build appropriate interfaces.
